item.title: Soden: Bord Bia chair 'kicking points for opposition'
item.description: As the IFA protest outside Bord Bia enters its fifth day, Poultry Chair Brendan Soden has called on the Chair of Bord Bia Larry Murrin to confirm if his companies import Brazilian chicken. The Co. Cavan farmer has called on Mr. Murrin to clarify the situation for Irish poultry farmers. He believes that poultry farmers in Brazil have little or no regulations compared to the EU. item.description: Gardaí are appealing for the public's assistance in tracing the whereabouts of Chloe Lawrence (17), who was reported missing from Emyvale, Co. Monaghan since Thursday 29th January 2026. She is described as being 5 feet 4 inches tall, with a slim build, light brown hair and blue eyes. Gardaí are concerned for Chloe’s wellbeing. item.title: 21 assaults on Gardai in local division last year
item.description: 21 assaults on members of An Garda Síochána were recorded in the Louth Cavan Monaghan Division during 2025. Figures released to Northern Sound also showed that nationally there was 344 assaults of Garda members over the past 12 months. The figures for the local Garda division also revealed that one member was injured by an animal, 2 were injured in a road collision and 7 members of the force were hurt during a trip or fall while on duty during 2025. item.title: Man arrested over alleged assault in Blacklion
item.description: A man has been arrested in relation to an alleged assault the occurred in Blacklion. Gardaí responded to an incident that occurred at approximately 7:15pm last night. The call out occurred in the Toam area of Blacklion. Advertisement A woman aged in her 60s received non-life threatening injuries that did not require medical treatment as a result of this incident. Gardaí say they later arrested the man and charged him in connection to the incident. He is set to appear before Cavan District Court

item.title: Frustration voiced over lack of road funding in Cavan
item.description: A local councillor has highlighted his frustration when it comes to the lack of funding allocated by Government towards road repairs across Co Cavan. Cllr TP O'Reilly has warned that roads are deteriorating at a rapid rate across Co Cavan, adding that he's never seen them as bad as they are now. According to the local Fianna Fail representative, Cavan County Council has not yet received an allocation from the Department on what it can spend on local roads this year. item.title: Local motorists urged to 'stay safe' ahead of bank holiday weekend
item.description: Local motorists are being urged to take care over the bank holiday weekend as roads remain wet following recent weather conditions. Flooding remains widespread across the region and more rain is expected in the coming days. Gardai across Cavan and Monaghan will be carrying out an enhanced Road Safety and Traffic Enforcement campaign across the St Brigid's bank holiday weekend with dedicated checkpoints in place. item.title: Cavan walking group goes from 'strength to strength'
item.description: A community initiative which was set up to combat loneliness and connect people of all ages and abilities together in Co Cavan has gone from strength to strength since its inception. 'Walkie, Talkie and Tea' was set up a number of months ago and is the brain child of local woman Ann Marie Sexton. With almost 30 members already, the group meets every Monday at 7:30pm at the Orchard Bar in Co Cavan. item.title: Contingency Plan for Leopardstown Saturday January 31
item.description: Following an inspection earlier today, the course at Leopardstown was found to be fit for racing. However, with the possibility of 10-20mm (approx) of rain forecast for tonight, there will be a further inspection of the course tomorrow, Saturday, at 8am. This will determine whether this meeting can go ahead as scheduled.
